questions.q: What is CRISPR, in the simplest terms?
a: A part of bacterial DNA that helps fight viruses
questions.why: Lesson 1 describes it as a natural defense in bacterial DNA.

questions.q: Which gene is named as a key part of the CRISPR system?
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists the Cas9 gene among three parts.

questions.q: What crop problem could gene editing address, per lesson 2?
questions.why: The summary says gene editing could end the disease devastating citrus plantations.

questions.q: What benefit came from the modified pigs in Canada?
a: Better digestion, reducing phosphorus in waste
questions.why: Lesson 2 says lower phosphorus waste reduces algal blooms.

questions.q: Which question concerns the ethics of gene editing in lesson 3?
a: Whether to choose a baby's gender or traits
questions.why: Lesson 3 asks if editing babies to be stronger or prettier is acceptable.
